mechanism_narrative: A continued drop in WORKPLACES mobility reduces midday and after-work shopping trips, so RETAIL_REC should fall further over the next four weeks. The mechanism is strongest when TRANSIT also declines, because fewer commuters reach shopping districts.
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES remains below its current level but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the commuting-to-shopping channel is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL mobility rises above its current elevated level, more time spent at home substitutes away from discretionary outings, pushing RETAIL_REC lower within one week and keeping it weaker over the next month.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL increases by at least 1 point week-on-week from the current baseline
failure_condition: If RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week but RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next 7 days, the home-stay substitution mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES indicates a broad mobility contraction that suppresses retail visits over the next two weeks. The effect should appear faster than in parks or grocery categories because discretionary shopping depends on external circulation.
failure_condition: If TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue to fall but RETAIL_REC stabilizes or increases over the next 14 days, the broad-contraction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls below its current level by another 5 points, the city is likely entering a stricter access regime that immediately depresses retail foot traffic. Retail mobility should weaken within one week of that crossing and stay lower over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls below -57.6 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: If TRANSIT crosses below -57.6 and RETAIL_REC does not fall within 7 days, the restriction-trigger mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent weakening in PARKS mobility relative to transit and workplaces signals lower overall out-of-home activity, which should translate into fewer incidental retail stops over the next four weeks. The effect is conditional on PARKS falling while the other two categories also remain depressed.
failure_condition: If PARKS keeps falling but RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days, the incidental-activity spillover mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM declines sharply, households consolidate errands and reduce total trip chaining, which pulls RETAIL_REC lower over the next two weeks. The signal should be strongest if the grocery decline is not matched by a compensating rise in TRANSIT.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM falls by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: If GROCERY_PHARM drops by at least 3 points week-on-week and RETAIL_REC does not decline over the next 14 days, the errand-consolidation mechanism fails.

mechanism_narrative: In warm-weather conditions, a rise in PARKS relative to RESIDENTIAL indicates substitution toward outdoor activities, which can offset indoor shopping and suppress RETAIL_REC over the next four weeks. The effect should not appear if parks and residential both rise together.
failure_condition: If PARKS rises while RESIDENTIAL does not fall and RETAIL_REC still increases over 28 days, the outdoor-substitution mechanism is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES drops below -40 percent from baseline, the labor market is sufficiently constrained that retail demand weakens again within two weeks. This threshold effect should persist only while TRANSIT remains near its current depressed range.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -40 percent change from baseline
failure_condition: If WORKPLACES falls below -40 and RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 14 days, or if TRANSIT rebounds sharply at the same time, the threshold channel is rejected.
